title: Journeyman utility fabric for telemetry-driven runbooks-as-tasks and contextual admin automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, composable 'Journeyman' utility fabric that converts telemetry and console context into safe, idempotent runbook tasks (actionlets) to accelerate incident remediation and routine admin work. This ticket captures the first engineering sprint: a prototype context-extractor + actionlet compiler + dry-run safety harness integrated with the Console trace timeline and the admin CLI.
rationale: Oncall engineers frequently reconstruct context from logs, traces and dashboards before running existing runbooks. By extracting structured context and turning runbook steps into parameterized tasks we can reduce time-to-remediate, lower operator errors, and enable reusable automation that stays within our safety constraints. This fills the space between free-form runbooks and fully autonomous remediations.
proposed_solution: 1) Context Extractor: a telemetry adapter that pulls relevant spans, recent Console traces, recent model-serving errors, and KV-cache metrics to produce a compact JSON context snapshot. 2) Actionlet Compiler: map snapshot + runbook templates (playlet DSL) -> ordered, idempotent tasks with typed inputs and precondition checks. 3) Safety Harness: dry-run mode, policy checks (RBAC + rate limits), and a sandboxable simulator for replaying steps against synthetic telemetry. 4) Integration: Console UI button to 'Prepare Journeyman run', and admin CLI flag --journeyman to surface suggested actionlets. 5) Telemetry: emit provenance traces and per-actionlet metrics for regression analysis.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype Context Extractor can generate a context snapshot from a sample incident (latency spike) via Console trace API.
- Compiler can translate one runbook template into a 3-step actionlet sequence with typed params.
- Dry-run reports precondition failures without mutating infra and logs deterministic execution plan.
- Console shows a one-click 'Prepare Journeyman run' that opens the suggested task list.
- End-to-end demo (video + lab guide) exists and engineering + oncall have reviewed.
- PR merged: backend + small Console UI; test coverage for extractor and compiler components.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing trace API for telemetry ingestion (Console traces v2).
- Store runbook templates in playlet format under infra/runbooks/playlets.
- Compiler should emit JSON-LD-like action descriptors (flat mapping) so downstream task runner can execute without schema nesting.
- Keep default behavior as suggestion-only; require explicit operator approval to execute any mutating actionlet.
- Prefer language-agnostic tooling: build extractor/compile pipeline as a small Go microservice with REST endpoints used by Console and admin CLI.
- Add feature flag ops.journeyman.enabled for controlled rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): internal engineering + SRE only, feature flag on; record metrics and feedback (2 weeks).
Phase 2: expand to customer-facing on-call teams; add RBAC scope checks and audits.
Phase 3: add automated regression detection (Optimize integration) and additional playlets.
Rollback: disable feature flag and revoke any queued actionlets; all changes are non-invasive until approved by operator.
risks:
- Incorrect context extraction may suggest wrong actions (mitigation: conservative precondition checks and human approval).
- Over-reliance on actionlets could bypass deeper debugging (mitigation: include strong provenance and links to raw traces).
- Security: actionlets may expose privileged operations (mitigation: RBAC + audit logs + KMS gating).
- UX confusion if suggestions are noisy (mitigation: limit suggestions to top-3 high-confidence actionlets).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for extractor transforms mapping traces -> snapshot.
- Integration test: pipeline end-to-end using a recorded incident trace.
- Dry-run safety tests to assert no side effects.
- User acceptance: internal oncall runbook drill following lab guide.
- Load test: validate extractor latency under peak telemetry ingestion (target < 300ms for snapshot generation).
